lines.text: Fifteen little squares, stacked like a staircase.
lines.caption: Fifteen little squares, stacked like a staircase.

lines.text: How many rectangles are hiding in here? Lots of kids say fifteen. <short pause> The real answer is way BIGGER.
lines.caption: How many rectangles are hiding in here? Lots of kids say fifteen. The real answer is way BIGGER.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count them all, together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count them all, together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Fifteen unit squares, in rows of five, four, three, two, one.
lines.caption: Fifteen unit squares, in rows of five, four, three, two, one.

lines.text: How many rectangles of any size are in the figure?
lines.caption: How many rectangles of any size are in the figure?

lines.text: And remember, squares count as rectangles too.
lines.caption: And remember, squares count as rectangles too.

lines.text: Is it fifteen, thirty-five, fifty-five, seventy, or seventy-five?
lines.caption: Is it fifteen, thirty-five, fifty-five, seventy, or seventy-five?

lines.text: So what are we really looking for?
lines.caption: So what are we really looking for?

lines.text: A rectangle here is a solid block of little squares.
lines.caption: A rectangle here is a solid block of little squares.

lines.text: It can be just one square, like this.
lines.caption: It can be just one square, like this.

lines.text: It can be a long strip, like this.
lines.caption: It can be a long strip, like this.

lines.text: Or a big block, like this one.
lines.caption: Or a big block, like this one.

lines.text: But it has to stay inside the stairs. This one sticks out, so it doesn't count.
lines.caption: But it has to stay inside the stairs. This one sticks out, so it doesn't count.

lines.text: Our job is to count them ALL, without missing any, and without counting any twice.
lines.caption: Our job is to count them ALL, without missing any, and without counting any twice.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Our first strategy is to sort the rectangles by height.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Our first strategy is to sort the rectangles by height.

lines.text: Let's start with the flat ones, just one row tall.
lines.caption: Let's start with the flat ones, just one row tall.

lines.text: Look at the bottom row. It has five squares.
lines.caption: Look at the bottom row. It has five squares.

lines.text: A strip one square long fits in five spots.
lines.caption: A strip one square long fits in five spots.

lines.text: A strip two squares long fits in four spots.
lines.caption: A strip two squares long fits in four spots.

lines.text: Length three fits in three spots. Length four in two spots. Length five in one spot.
lines.caption: Length three fits in three spots. Length four in two spots. Length five in one spot.

lines.text: So a row of five holds five, plus four, plus three, plus two, plus one. That's fifteen.
lines.caption: So a row of five holds five, plus four, plus three, plus two, plus one. That's fifteen.

lines.text: The same idea works for every row. The row of four holds ten. Then six, three, and one.
lines.caption: The same idea works for every row. The row of four holds ten. Then six, three, and one.

lines.text: Add up the rows: thirty-five.
lines.caption: Add up the rows: thirty-five.

lines.text: Now for rectangles two rows tall.
lines.caption: Now for rectangles two rows tall.

lines.text: Can a two-row rectangle reach the fifth column? No! The second row has no square there.
lines.caption: Can a two-row rectangle reach the fifth column? No! The second row has no square there.

lines.text: So the bottom two rows act like a strip of four.
lines.caption: So the bottom two rows act like a strip of four.

lines.text: Here's the rule. A band of rows is only as wide as its TOP row.
lines.caption: Here's the rule. A band of rows is only as wide as its TOP row.

lines.text: The two-row bands are four, three, two, and one wide. So ten, plus six, plus three, plus one. Twenty!
lines.caption: The two-row bands are four, three, two, and one wide. So ten, plus six, plus three, plus one. Twenty!

lines.text: Three rows tall: six, plus three, plus one. That's ten.
lines.caption: Three rows tall: six, plus three, plus one. That's ten.

lines.text: Four rows tall: three, plus one. That's four.
lines.caption: Four rows tall: three, plus one. That's four.

lines.text: Five rows tall: just one, the tall column on the left.
lines.caption: Five rows tall: just one, the tall column on the left.

lines.text: Now add them all up. Thirty-five, plus twenty, plus ten, plus four, plus one. <short pause> That's seventy rectangles!
lines.caption: Now add them all up. Thirty-five, plus twenty, plus ten, plus four, plus one. That's seventy rectangles!

lines.text: Now here's a faster way. I call it the corner trick.
lines.caption: Now here's a faster way. I call it the corner trick.

lines.text: Every rectangle is set by two squares: its top-right square, and its bottom-left square.
lines.caption: Every rectangle is set by two squares: its top-right square, and its bottom-left square.

lines.text: So let's pick a top-right square. Say, the one in column three, row two.
lines.caption: So let's pick a top-right square. Say, the one in column three, row two.

lines.text: Where can the bottom-left square go? Anywhere in this block, up to our square.
lines.caption: Where can the bottom-left square go? Anywhere in this block, up to our square.

lines.text: That's three columns times two rows. Six choices, so six rectangles! Even our square on its own counts.
lines.caption: That's three columns times two rows. Six choices, so six rectangles! Even our square on its own counts.

lines.text: They all fit, because everything below and to the left of a square is inside the stairs.
lines.caption: They all fit, because everything below and to the left of a square is inside the stairs.

lines.text: So each square gets its column number, times its row number. Let's write that in every square.
lines.caption: So each square gets its column number, times its row number. Let's write that in every square.

lines.text: Now add each column. The first column is one, plus two, plus three, plus four, plus five. That's fifteen.
lines.caption: Now add each column. The first column is one, plus two, plus three, plus four, plus five. That's fifteen.

lines.text: The second column is two, plus four, plus six, plus eight. That's twenty.
lines.caption: The second column is two, plus four, plus six, plus eight. That's twenty.

lines.text: Then three, plus six, plus nine is eighteen. Four plus eight is twelve. And the last column is five.
lines.caption: Then three, plus six, plus nine is eighteen. Four plus eight is twelve. And the last column is five.

lines.text: Fifteen, plus twenty, plus eighteen, plus twelve, plus five. Seventy again!
lines.caption: Fifteen, plus twenty, plus eighteen, plus twelve, plus five. Seventy again!

lines.text: When should you use the corner trick? When the stairs get tall. You just fill in a times table!
lines.caption: When should you use the corner trick? When the stairs get tall. You just fill in a times table!

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Fifteen counts only the little unit squares.
lines.caption: Fifteen counts only the little unit squares.

lines.text: Thirty-five counts only the flat strips, one row tall.
lines.caption: Thirty-five counts only the flat strips, one row tall.

lines.text: Fifty-five counts only the thin strips, lying flat or standing up. It misses the fat blocks.
lines.caption: Fifty-five counts only the thin strips, lying flat or standing up. It misses the fat blocks.

lines.text: Seventy-five is too many. Stretch the bottom band of two rows to five wide, and you add five that stick out.
lines.caption: Seventy-five is too many. Stretch the bottom band of two rows to five wide, and you add five that stick out.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a taller staircase.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a taller staircase.

lines.text: Now the rows have six, five, four, three, two, and one squares.
lines.caption: Now the rows have six, five, four, three, two, and one squares.

lines.text: How many rectangles are in this one?
lines.caption: How many rectangles are in this one?

lines.text: Use the corner trick!
lines.caption: Use the corner trick!

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. In every square, write its column number times its row number.
lines.caption: Let's check. In every square, write its column number times its row number.

lines.text: Add each column: twenty-one, thirty, thirty, twenty-four, fifteen, six.
lines.caption: Add each column: twenty-one, thirty, thirty, twenty-four, fifteen, six.

lines.text: Twenty-one, plus thirty, plus thirty, plus twenty-four, plus fifteen, plus six. <short pause> That's one hundred twenty-six!
lines.caption: Twenty-one, plus thirty, plus thirty, plus twenty-four, plus fifteen, plus six. That's one hundred twenty-six!

lines.text: If you found all one hundred twenty-six rectangles, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found all one hundred twenty-six rectangles, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Every rectangle is pinned down by its top-right and bottom-left squares.
lines.caption: Every rectangle is pinned down by its top-right and bottom-left squares.

lines.text: For each top-right square, count spots for the bottom-left, then add.
lines.caption: For each top-right square, count spots for the bottom-left, then add.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep counting, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep counting, and I'll see you next time!
